method.leafEnumeration: A JSON scanner that records the byte-exact text span of every scalar was used, so a mutation replaces ONE token and leaves every other byte of the document identical (2538 -> 2538.0). No re-serialisation, no reformatting, therefore no whole-document byte drift that could masquerade as a guard firing. The scanner's parse is asserted equal to json.loads on every document before use.
method.whatCountsAsAnIntegerLeaf: A JSON number with no fraction or exponent. JSON booleans are EXCLUDED even though isinstance(True, int) is True in the host language; they are swept separately as the bool arm.
mutations: float arm: every integer leaf, one at a time, token -> token + '.0'.
bool arm: every integer leaf whose value is 0 or 1, one at a time, 1 -> true and 0 -> false. True == 1 and False == 0 are the other half of the same equivalence class.
method.invocation: python3 -I -B <checker>, with cwd at the copied repository root and no arguments, so the checker resolves its own declared candidate at HERE/BINDING exactly as it does in normal use. The contract was restored after every run.

threeOutcomeClassification.REJECTED-BY-POSITION: non-zero AND at least one finding line identifies the mutated leaf -- by full JSON path, or by its key together with an ancestor key, the substituted spelling, or uniqueness of that key in the document. The guard at the position fired.
threeOutcomeClassification.REJECTED-COLLATERAL: non-zero for a reason that does not identify the mutated leaf. The guard at the position did NOT fire; the position is effectively unguarded and the exit code is not evidence of a defence.
threeOutcomeClassification.whyThisMatters: A non-zero exit is not evidence a guard fired. This trap has bitten twice already in this corpus. Every non-zero result here was classified from its finding TEXT, not from its exit code.

collateralSubKinds.global-type-gate: a raw-parser rule that forbids the substituted type anywhere in the document (FloatForbidden / 'float forbidden'). It does not localise, but it is a real defence and is reported separately rather than being presented as an unguarded position.
collateralSubKinds.candidate-digest: the checker pins the sha256 of its own candidate and refuses any edited bytes before looking at values. Also a real block, also non-localising, and it means the checker demonstrates nothing about type discipline for any candidate other than the exact pinned one.
collateralSubKinds.unrelated: the rejection came from arithmetic the mutation perturbed elsewhere -- typically a self-census counter. NOT a defence. See collateralIsNotADefence below.

method.handAdjudication: The automatic position-naming test was applied to every rejected run, and then every run it placed in the 'unrelated' collateral bucket was read individually. Where the finding did identify the position in prose that the matcher could not see, the verdict was overridden to REJECTED-BY-POSITION and the justifying finding text was recorded. 7 overrides in the control pair, 28 in check-c2-v5.py, 12 in check-evaluation-proof-v11.py; 0 elsewhere. No override moved anything INTO the collateral bucket, and no ADMITTED verdict was ever adjusted.

method.pinCoverageProbe: A checker may pin several inputs and the susceptible one need not be the declared candidate. For every .json file each checker names in its source, two screening probes were run: (a) replace the file with {"garbage": 1} and see whether the exit code changes -- if it does not, the file is not load-bearing and cannot be an attack surface; (b) float-substitute one leading and one mid-document integer leaf. Result: for every checker probed, the ONLY load-bearing input that admits a float substitution is the checker's own declared candidate. Two files that admitted (retention-tiers.v12.json under check-retention-custody-v22.py and evidence.v8.json under check-trusted-request-context-v3.py) were shown by the garbage probe not to be read at all. The declared pairing in the task brief is therefore the right pairing, by measurement rather than assumption. isThisSystemic.verdict: SYSTEMIC. Not uniform as an outcome, but systemic as a class, and the majority of the measured corpus is susceptible.
isThisSystemic.reasoning: The corpus does not share one defect; it shares the absence of a shared rule. Each artifact reinvents type discipline independently, so coverage is a per-author accident. Five distinct designs were measured, with five different outcomes, and no artifact inherits its neighbour's protection. The measured split is between the deeply revised high-version successors (check-d9-v1.14.py, check-evaluation-proof-v10/v11.py, check-evidence-v10.py, check-retention-custody-v22.py), which hold across every leaf swept, and the low-version foundational checkers (check-claims.py, check-delivery.py, check-fact-plane.py, check-fact-identity.py, check-resolved-inputs.py, check-versioning-v8.py, check-product-dispositions.py, check-method-dispositions.py, check-retention-v3.py, check-scope-correction-a3-v5.py), which admit on the first or second leaf a screen touches. Whether that split is caused by revision depth, by author, or by anything else is NOT measured here -- only the split itself is.

designsObserved.rawParserTypeBan: check-retention-custody-v22.py and check-r1-v1.5.py reject floats at parse time before any semantic layer. This is the only design that is total for the type it bans -- 271/271 and 64/64 float rejections respectively. It is also the only design that generalises without per-position work. But it bans only what it enumerates: R1 bans floats and not booleans, and 40 of its 52 boolean positions are admitted.
designsObserved.perPositionExactType: check-d9-v1.14.py, check-evaluation-proof-v10.py and check-evaluation-proof-v11.py compare types exactly at each position and name the position when they reject. 0 admissions and 0 collateral across 110, 96 and 131 runs. This is the strongest measured result: total AND localising.
designsObserved.deriveAndCompareExactly: check-evidence-v10.py derives the whole expected successor from pinned authority and compares it exactly, so every respelling is reported as 'expected 0, found 0.0' or 'found True' with the path. Total and localising like the per-position design, and it needs no list of guarded positions -- but it only works for a document that is fully derivable from its inputs.
designsObserved.wholeCandidateDigest: check-operability-v10.py pins the sha256 of its own candidate. 105/105 rejected, 0 admitted, but 0 by position: it never looks at a value. It blocks this attack on the pinned bytes and demonstrates nothing about any other candidate.
designsObserved.registeredPositionsOnly: check-c2-v4.py and check-c2-v5.py enumerate the positions they guard. Both have admissions, because enumeration is a list and lists go stale. This is the design that produced LB-C2-01 twice.
designsObserved.none: check-trusted-request-context-v3.py has no observed type discipline at any integer leaf: 3 of 3 float and 1 of 1 bool admitted, 100 percent of its integer surface. The 10 older current-head checkers in the broader screen are in the same category, and worse: they admit respellings inside files they treat as pinned authority, not only in their own candidate.

isThisSystemic.unpinnedAuthorityIsTheWiderProblem: Among the nine exhaustively swept pairs, every non-candidate input is digest-pinned, so a respelling there is refused. Among the 11 screened older checkers that is not true, and the admitted inputs are SHARED. Measured multiplicity of the screened admissions: resolved-inputs.v2.json admitted by 4 checkers; d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json, delivery.v2.json, fact-plane.v1.json, threat-model.v3.json and product-dispositions.v1.json by 3 each; claim-register.v1.json and c2-plan-stage-schema.v3.json by 2 each. One edit to one shared upstream document is therefore admitted by several checkers at once, and none of them is the document's own checker.
isThisSystemic.secondOrderFinding: The bool arm is systematically weaker than the float arm. Across the 9 non-control pairs, floats are admitted at 16 of 869 positions (1.8%) but booleans at 41 of 208 (19.7%). Two artifacts (check-r1-v1.5.py, check-retention-custody-v22.py) close the float half completely with a parser-level ban and one of them leaves the boolean half wide open. An author who reasons 'floats are the LB-C2-01 defect' closes exactly half of the equivalence class.
isThisSystemic.thirdOrderFinding: check-c2-v5.py's authoring-time sweep of its predecessor was performed by calling V4.check() in-process, not by running the checker. That produced 57 admissions, which happens to match the process-level number exactly -- but the method cannot see any layer outside check(), so the agreement is luck rather than evidence. The end-to-end process sweep recorded here is the first measurement of that number that the number's own claim ('exit 0, full green banner') actually supports.
isThisSystemic.whatWouldActuallyFixIt: Not more per-position guards -- enumeration is the design that failed twice. Two measured designs need no list of guarded positions: the raw-parser type ban (total, but only over the types it enumerates -- R1 banned floats and left booleans open) and whole-candidate derivation (total and localising, but only available for a document fully derivable from its inputs). A corpus rule would have to combine them: a SHARED loader that rejects, at parse time, every JSON scalar whose host type is not the declared type, for ALL ==-equivalent spellings -- float AND bool at minimum -- so no artifact has to remember. This is measurement-derived inference, not a repair: nothing was changed, and no disposition is claimed.

notableSecondaryObservations: check-c2-v4.py rejects 0 of 66 bool substitutions by exit code, but 50 of those 66 rejections are census-drift collateral and were demonstrated above to be neutralisable with two extra edits. Its measured bool exposure is therefore far larger than its exit codes suggest.

check-operability-v10.py's whole-candidate digest pin means the checker cannot validate any candidate but the one it already has. Its 105 rejections are byte-identity refusals, not type checks; a re-authored operability.v11 would inherit no type discipline from it.

Under --selftest, the deepest mode these artifacts offer, the admitted positions stay admitted: check-c2-v5.py 13/13; check-r1-v1.5.py 40/40; check-trusted-request-context-v3.py 4/4. check-c2-v5.py --selftest additionally printed SELFTEST-PASS over the mutated document.

whatIDidNotCheck: Any checker other than the ten swept in perPair and the seventeen baselined in broaderScreenOfOtherCurrentHeadCheckers. docs/coop/artifacts contains 81 check-*.py files; 54 were never executed at all. The nine named pairs plus the control were swept EXHAUSTIVELY; the other seventeen were only SCREENED (two leaves per load-bearing input) and six of those seventeen could not be screened because they already exit non-zero on the unmodified tree. Superseded versions (check-evidence-v4..v9, check-retention-custody-v11..v21, check-d9-v1.7..v1.13, check-operability-v3..v9, check-evaluation-proof-v6..v9, check-c2.py, check-r1.py, check-trusted-request-context-v1..v2 and the rest) are UNMEASURED.

Any ADMITTED COUNT for the seventeen screened checkers. The screen touches two integer leaves per input and stops; it establishes THAT a checker admits, and at which position, but not HOW MANY of its leaves admit. No count is published for them, and none should be inferred from the 31/39 pair figure -- that is a count of checker/input pairs in which a screened leaf was admitted, not of admitted positions.

Type substitutions other than float and bool. A string '2538', a null, an exponent spelling 2.538e3, a leading-plus '+2538', '2538.000', or a Decimal-bearing parser hook were not tried. The equivalence class '== the declared integer but not the declared type' is larger than the two spellings measured here, so every ADMITTED count in this document is a LOWER bound on the exposure.

Multi-leaf mutations, except the single three-edit demonstration recorded under collateralIsNotADefence. A co-edited attack that corrects the counters it perturbs was not swept; the REJECTED-COLLATERAL counts are therefore also lower bounds on exposure, not upper bounds on safety.
Non-JSON inputs. Several checkers read .md files (ARCHITECTURE-TO-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md and others). No .md input was mutated.

The pin-coverage probe is a TWO-LEAF SCREEN per referenced JSON file, not a sweep. A checker could pin the first and middle integer leaf of an input and leave a third unpinned; that would not appear here. It was also not run for check-evidence-v10.py, whose ~130s runtime made a 3-probe-per-input screen over its 24 pinned inputs cost more than the main sweep; check-evidence-v10.py's non-candidate inputs are therefore UNMEASURED for pin coverage.

Source-level proof of mechanism. Every classification in this document is behavioural -- derived from exit codes and finding text. No claim is made about which line of which checker did or did not fire, except where the checker's own finding says so.

Whether an admitted position is semantically exploitable beyond producing exit 0 with a green banner. That is the criterion the adjudication of check-c2-v4.py used, and it is the criterion used here; downstream consequence was not modelled.
Checker modes other than the default invocation, except the --selftest re-runs explicitly recorded per pair. --machine, --emit-candidate and positional-argument invocations were not swept.
Concurrency and TOCTOU behaviour, filesystem interposition, and any property that is not a function of the candidate's bytes.
